reason: The cited evidence directly supports the existence of hot ductility loss in HEAs and the inapplicability of thermo-mechanical processing for SLM. It also mentions SEGB as a possible approach involving post heat treatment. However, the evidence does not provide any specific prior demonstration that SEGB formation improves elevated-temperature ductility or yield strength in HEAs, which is the core mechanistic premise of the hypothesis.
premises: HEAs exhibit significant hot ductility loss (e.g., 50-75% strain drop) at 400-750°C
Thermo-mechanical processing is inapplicable as a post-processing step for SLM components
Serrated grain boundaries (SEGB) can be introduced via post heat treatment involving second-phase interactions
